questions.text: The Internet is a worldwide collection of ___.
questions.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide collection of networks.

questions.text: The Internet originated as ___ in September 1969.
questions.explanation: ARPANET was the origin of the Internet.

questions.text: An IP address is a number that uniquely identifies a ___.
options: Computer or device connected to the Internet
questions.explanation: An IP address uniquely identifies a computer or device on the Internet.

questions.text: A domain name is the ___ version of an IP address.
questions.explanation: A domain name is the text version of an IP address.

questions.text: DNS stands for ___.
questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System.

questions.text: Which server translates a domain name into its associated IP address?
questions.explanation: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.text: A Web browser is a program that allows users to ___.
questions.explanation: A Web browser allows users to access Web pages.

questions.text: The first page that a Web site displays is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The home page is the first page a Web site displays.

questions.text: A Web page has a unique address called a ___.
questions.explanation: A Web page's unique address is its URL.

questions.text: A program used to find Web pages pertaining to a specific topic is a ___.
questions.explanation: A search engine locates Web pages on a specific topic.

questions.text: The process of receiving information from the Internet to your computer is called ___.
questions.explanation: Downloading is the process of receiving information.

questions.text: The process of transferring data in a continuous and even flow is called ___.
questions.explanation: Streaming transfers data in a continuous and even flow.

questions.text: E-mail is the transmission of ___ via a computer network.
questions.explanation: E-mail is the transmission of messages and files via a network.

questions.text: An e-mail program allows you to create, send, receive, forward, store, print and ___ e-mail messages.
questions.explanation: An e-mail program allows deleting e-mail messages too.

questions.text: Instant messaging (IM) is a ___ Internet communications service.
questions.explanation: Instant messaging is a real-time Internet service.

questions.text: A chat room is a location on an Internet server that permits users to ___.
questions.explanation: A chat room permits users to chat with each other.

questions.text: VoIP enables users to ___.
options: Speak to other users over the Internet
questions.explanation: VoIP lets users speak to each other over the Internet.

questions.text: VoIP is also called ___.
questions.explanation: VoIP is also known as Internet telephony.

questions.text: FTP stands for ___.
questions.explanation: FTP is File Transfer Protocol.

questions.text: A newsgroup is an online area in which users ___.
options: Have written discussions about a particular subject
questions.explanation: A newsgroup hosts written discussions about a subject.

questions.text: A LAN is a network that connects computers and devices in a ___.
questions.explanation: A LAN covers a limited geographical area.

questions.text: Which network covers a large geographical area?
questions.explanation: A WAN covers a large geographical area.

questions.text: A network that connects LANs in a metropolitan area such as a city is a ___.
questions.explanation: A MAN connects LANs in a metropolitan area.

questions.text: A wireless LAN (WLAN) is a LAN that uses ___.
questions.explanation: A WLAN uses no physical wires.

questions.text: The layout of the computers and devices in a communications network is called the network ___.
questions.explanation: Network topology is the layout of computers and devices on a network.

questions.text: Which communications device transmits data to its correct destination on a network?
questions.explanation: A router sends data to its correct destination on a network.

questions.text: The amount of data that can travel over a communications channel is called the ___.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can travel over a channel.

questions.text: Wi-Fi is based on the ___ standard.
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is based on the 802.11 standard.

questions.text: Wi-Fi is sometimes referred to as ___.
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is sometimes called wireless Ethernet.

questions.text: Which technology uses short-range radio waves to transmit data between two devices?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth uses short-range radio waves to transmit data.

questions.text: A cybercrime is an ___ illegal act.
questions.explanation: A cybercrime is an online or Internet-based illegal act.

questions.text: Which malicious program duplicates itself and attacks the computer system?
questions.explanation: A virus duplicates itself and attacks the computer system.

questions.text: Which software detects and removes viruses from a computer?
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects and removes viruses.

questions.text: The technique intruders use to make their network or Internet transmission appear legitimate is ___.
questions.explanation: Spoofing makes transmissions appear legitimate.

questions.text: The process of converting readable data into unreadable characters to prevent unauthorized access is called ___.
questions.explanation: Encryption converts readable data into unreadable characters.

questions.text: An encrypted code attached to an electronic message to verify the identity of the sender is a ___.
questions.explanation: A digital signature verifies the identity of the sender.

questions.text: A small text file that a Web server stores on your computer is a ___.
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small text file stored by a Web server.

questions.text: Unsolicited e-mail messages sent to many recipients are called ___.
questions.explanation: Spam is unsolicited e-mail sent in bulk.

questions.text: Which scam sends an official-looking e-mail message that attempts to obtain your personal and financial information?
questions.explanation: Phishing uses official-looking e-mails to obtain personal information.

questions.text: A firewall protects a network's resources from ___.
questions.explanation: A firewall protects network resources from intrusion.

questions.text: The process of restricting access to certain material on the Web is called ___.
questions.explanation: Content filtering restricts access to certain Web material.

questions.text: Which device authenticates a person's identity by translating a personal characteristic into a digital code?
questions.explanation: A biometric device authenticates identity using personal characteristics.

questions.text: A duplicate of a file, program or disk that can be used if the original is lost or damaged is a ___.
questions.explanation: A backup is a duplicate used when the original is lost.

questions.text: Which of the following protects a computer from electrical power variations?
questions.explanation: Surge protectors and UPS protect against power variations.

questions.text: ___ is an applied science devoted to incorporating comfort, efficiency and safety into the design of items in the workplace.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics incorporates comfort, efficiency and safety in workplace design.

questions.text: Computer ethics are the ___ that govern the use of computers and information systems.
questions.explanation: Computer ethics are moral guidelines for computer use.

questions.text: Green computing involves ___.
options: Reducing electricity and environmental waste while using a computer
questions.explanation: Green computing reduces electricity and environmental waste.

questions.text: Which of the following is a health concern resulting from the widespread use of computers?
questions.explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a known computer-related health concern.

questions.text: The right of individuals to deny or restrict the collection and use of information about them is called ___.
questions.explanation: Information privacy is the right to restrict collection and use of personal information.

questions.text: A sacrificial computer system intended to attract cyberattacks is known as a ___.
questions.explanation: A honeypot is a sacrificial system used to attract cyberattacks.

questions.text: Which shortcut key cuts selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+X is the shortcut for cutting selected text.

questions.text: Which shortcut key copies selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C is the shortcut for copying selected text.

questions.text: Which shortcut key pastes copied or cut text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+V is the shortcut for pasting text.

questions.text: The shortcut key used to right-align a paragraph in MS Word is ___.
questions.explanation: Ctrl+R right-aligns a paragraph in MS Word.

questions.text: Word documents are saved with the file extension ___.
questions.explanation: Word documents are saved with the .docx extension.

questions.text: In MS Word, the Find and Replace commands are located in the ___ group of the Home tab.
questions.explanation: Find and Replace are in the Editing group of the Home tab.

questions.text: Which MS Word feature changes text from lowercase to UPPERCASE?
questions.explanation: Change Case changes text between cases such as UPPERCASE.

questions.text: In MS Excel, columns are identified by ___.
questions.explanation: Excel columns are identified by letters.

questions.text: Which Excel function adds up a range of numbers?
questions.explanation: The SUM function adds up a range of numbers.

questions.text: The Excel shortcut keys for inserting the SUM (AutoSum) function are ___.
questions.explanation: Alt + = inserts the AutoSum function in Excel.

questions.text: The NOT function in Excel ___.
options: Returns TRUE if all conditions are true
Changes TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE
questions.explanation: The NOT function reverses TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE.

questions.text: Which Excel function removes unnecessary spaces from a string of text?
questions.explanation: The TRIM function removes unnecessary spaces from text.

questions.text: To add a border to a cell in Excel, you click the Border list arrow on the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: The Border command is on the Home tab in Excel.

questions.text: Which tab in Excel contains the Sort & Filter commands?
questions.explanation: The Sort & Filter group is on the Data tab.

questions.text: To create a chart from selected data in Excel, you use the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: Charts are created using the Insert tab in Excel.

questions.text: The Excel Wrap Text command is located on the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: Wrap Text is on the Home tab in Excel.

questions.text: To fit a worksheet to print on one page, use the Fit to option in the ___ dialog box.
questions.explanation: The Fit to option is found in the Page Setup dialog box.

questions.text: Which Excel function returns the current date and time?
questions.explanation: The NOW function returns the current date and time.

questions.text: In Gmail, which button is used to attach a file to an e-mail?
questions.explanation: The Attach button, shown with a paperclip icon, attaches files in Gmail.

questions.text: PowerPoint presentations are saved with the file extension ___.
questions.explanation: PowerPoint presentations use the .pptx file extension.
